claims.statement: Conversation carries identity (contact_id + channel_identity_id FKs RESTRICT/RESTRICT; zalo_chat_id nullable unique), mode (BOT|HUMAN|CLOSED) and status (OPEN), the per-conversation bot lock (bot_locked_until + bot_lock_owner UUID + bot_lock_heartbeat_at) with Settings.bot_lock_ttl_seconds=180, bookkeeping (version, conversation_seq, taken_over_at, assigned_recruiter_id, unread_count), and follow-up state (followup_count, last_followup_at, followup_opted_out).

conversation_seq is a strictly monotonic counter that increments on every mutation and is observability-only; version is the optimistic-lock token and intentionally skips bot outcomes to avoid invalidating in-flight optimistic-lock guards.

The lock policy in app/conversation_messaging/domain/ownership.py is pure: normalize_lock_owner handles UUID|str|None, lock_owner_matches returns True when expected is None or matches as strings, lock_still_live normalizes naive datetimes to UTC; run_turn calls recheck_ownership after svc.get and db.refresh so a False yields outcome=suppressed reason=lock_owner_lost without calling the agent.

DeliveryState is forward-only: PENDING/SENDING/SEND_UNKNOWN/FAILED/SUPPRESSED share rank 0, SENT=1, DELIVERED=2, READ=3; delivery_rank and receipt_advances keep the policy pure so a delivery or read receipt only updates when it advances the rank and never regresses.

The outbound dispatcher tick (run_outbound_dispatch_tick on Settings.reconcile_interval_seconds, registered via register_unique_tick) calls recover_outbound_batch which dispatches PENDING outbox rows and finalizes SENDING rows past the stale threshold without resending; failures are isolated per command via on_failure(candidate, exc).

take_over atomically sets mode=HUMAN, status=OPEN, assigned_recruiter_id=recruiter.id, taken_over_at=now, clears needs_human + unread_count + the bot lock entirely (bot_locked_until/bot_lock_owner/bot_lock_heartbeat_at = NULL), bumps version + conversation_seq, records a SYSTEM message and an audit row tagged take_over_conversation, and publishes a conversation_updated event.

Two recruiters racing on the same unassigned conversation produce exactly one winner and one ConversationConflict because every transition uses a conditional UPDATE guarded by the optimistic-lock version; release/semi_auto/close/reopen follow the same pattern with state-specific guards (e.g. non-admin release requires ownership or unowned-without-needs_human).

_SEMI_AUTO_INACTIVITY = timedelta(minutes=5) is the staleness bound for semi-auto mode: a recruiter stays assigned but the bot also replies to simple intents, with bot silence on escalation intents after 5 minutes without a recruiter message.
All state mutations funnel through record_audit and the ConversationEventsPort (events.py) so the recruiter console sees the change via the realtime bridge and the audit table records who did what.
